Done. All checks pass.

**Changes**

- `version.ts` (new): `export const PLUGIN_VERSION = "0.3.1"` — a compile-time literal the bundler inlines into `host.mjs`, since BB ships the host bundle without `package.json`.
- `host.ts`: imports `PLUGIN_VERSION` from `./version.js`; deleted `pluginVersion()` (which read `./package.json` and silently fell back to `"0.1.0"`) and its `fileURLToPath` import; all four call sites now use the constant.
- `server.ts`: `bb.background.service("runtime-warmup")` calls host `status` on every connected host once at plugin start and every 10 minutes — `status` triggers `ensureRuntime` host-side, so each machine installs the matching runtime without the settings screen. Per-host and outer errors are caught and logged via `bb.log.debug`; the interval clears on service abort (plugin dispose/reload).
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json`: bumped to `0.3.1`.
- `tests/version.test.mjs` (new): asserts `PLUGIN_VERSION` equals `package.json` version and that `host.ts` imports `./version` with no `package.json` read and no `"0.1.0"` literal.

Invariants held: `deriveProviderOptions` and the Agent command setting are untouched; the warm-up never throws.

**Verification**: `node /tmp/muse-version/check.mjs "$PWD"` → OK; `node --test tests/version.test.mjs tests/runtime-install.test.mjs` → 8/8 pass; `npm run typecheck` → clean.

APPROACH: Replaced the runtime `package.json` read in host.ts with a compile-time `PLUGIN_VERSION` literal in a new version.ts (bundlers inline it into the shipped host.mjs). Added a lifecycle-managed `bb.background.service` in server.ts that pings host `status` on every connected host at start and every 10 min, letting the host-side `ensureRuntime` install the correct runtime with no UI visit. Bumped package.json/lockfile to 0.3.1 and added a sync-guard test.

LESSON: Code running inside a bundled host artifact must never resolve files relative to `import.meta.url` — the bundle ships alone. Keep version as a literal in a tiny module and guard it with a test against package.json so future bumps don't drift.
